description: Real EUR-Lex captures and targeted parser regression fixtures, one per format era or reported edge case, frozen as gzipped fixtures. This file is the map of the EU document-format versions LegalViz has to handle; the paired corpus-fixtures.test.js asserts each still parses into articles/recitals so a parser change can't silently regress an era. Counts below are the parse output at freeze time; tests assert `>=` these floors, so parser improvements are free but regressions fail. To refresh or extend, drop a new `<kind>-<era>-<CELEX>.<ext>.gz` here (FMX: xml, EUR-Lex HTML: html) and add an entry. A capture must hold the act exactly once — Cellar manifestation duplication has silently inflated recital counts here before, and shared/corpus-fixtures.test.js now asserts the parse-health signals in search/parse-health.js against every fixture to catch it. Era fixtures are sourced from the gitignored local corpus (backend/search/data/laws{,-html}); HTML fixtures are the raw EUR-Lex HTML the live viewer reparses.

fixtures.note: Earliest bulk-FMX era (pre-2005). isFmxDocument() returns false for the bare <GENERAL> shape, but wrapForParsing() normalises it and recitals + articles parse. Small v2 acts use <ENACTING.TERMS> (this fixture); large structured v2 acts (e.g. Directive 2004/18/EC) instead nest the body under <CONTENTS> — the parser falls back to that container so their articles parse too (guarded by a synthetic test in fmxParser.test.js). Re-frozen for issue #142: the original capture held three identical <PUBLICATION> OJ stubs and three identical copies of the <ACT>, so it parsed 6 recitals against the act’s real 2.
Single-root <ACT> document; the canonical mid-era FMX shape.

Mid-to-late FMX shape. Also references Directive 2001/18/EC and the TFEU, so it guards external-law + treaty cross-reference extraction. Re-frozen for issue #142: the original capture concatenated the same <ACT> twice, so it parsed 56 recitals against the act’s real 28 and the floor here locked that in. The multi-root <ACT>+<ACT> wrapping this fixture used to cover is guarded synthetically in fmxParser.test.js instead — a duplicated capture is not a document shape worth freezing.
Newest FMX wrapper: the ACT is nested under an <OJ>/<PUBLICATION> envelope. Parser must descend past the envelope to the ACT.

fixtures.format: EUR-Lex HTML — <TXT_TE> plaintext, ECSC High Authority decision
fixtures.note: Oldest HTML shape: <TXT_TE> body with numbered articles and unnumbered preamble. No FMX exists for these acts.
Pre-1990s directives with a run of unnumbered 'Whereas …' paragraphs between the 'Having regard to …' citations and 'HAS ADOPTED THIS DIRECTIVE:'. Parsed by parseWhereasRecitals.
Amending regulation with a 'SOLE ARTICLE' label instead of a numbered 'Article N' heading. Recovered as a lone Article 1 by the single-provision fallback.

fixtures.format: EUR-Lex HTML — <TXT_TE>, single-provision decision, no article heading
fixtures.note: Operative text follows the enacting formula directly with no article heading at all; salvaged as Article 1. Has no recitals (correct — none in the source).

Directive 95/46/EC. 1990s acts number recitals '(N) Whereas …' under a 'Having regard to …' block with no standalone 'Whereas:' heading; the whole preamble must be scanned. This is the regression that motivated the fixture library. Also the guard for HTML cross-reference extraction: recital preambles get cross-ref links injected, the crossReferences map is populated, and trailing '(N) OJ No L …' footnote lines are captured as OJ references. Its Article 2 is the definitions guard for the pre-2000 drafting style: eight points written in the 'term' shall mean … form, one of them (the data subject's consent) with an apostrophe inside the term.

fixtures.format: EUR-Lex HTML — <TXT_TE> with TITLE divisions and a trailing ANNEX
fixtures.note: Regulation with TITLE I–IV chapter structure and an annex after the articles. Guards annex extraction in the plaintext branch (which previously dropped annexes and let their content bleed into the last article) plus TITLE-level division parsing.
Targeted parser fixture for Article 27's bare `Depreciation shall be understood as …` definition wording.
Targeted parser fixture for quoted amendment labels that must not be promoted to definitions by the fallback grammar.
